transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve just been having a really hard time lately. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I keep thinking it might be better if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes I feel like… like dying would be what I deserve, like a fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and the people I work with. I know that probably sounds awful.
Did something specific happen recently that led to you feeling this way?

I’m not sure there was one specific thing, honestly. I’ve been trying to figure that out because I know it would make more sense if I could point to something, but… it feels like it’s just been building. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming anyone or being dramatic. I just kind of reached a point where it felt heavier than usual, if that makes sense.
Has there been a major stressful change or event in your life recently?

I mean… I guess the big thing was my husband’s back injury. That was about a year and five months ago, and since then he’s been mostly stuck at home. I don’t know if that counts as “recent” exactly, but that’s when things really started to change for us.
Do you feel like your worsening mood has mainly been a reaction to your husband’s injury and the changes that came with it?

I think it probably is connected, yeah. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m blaming his injury or anything… but the depression really settled in a few months after that happened. So it’s been, I guess, about a year and two months now that I’ve felt this way.
During this past year, was there a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed nearly every day?

Yeah… yes, I think so. Honestly it’s been a lot longer than two weeks. It’s been kind of with me most days for about a year and two months now, since a few months after my husband got hurt. I don’t know if I’m saying that the right way, but it hasn’t really lifted for any real stretch of time.
Before this past year, had you ever gone through another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for weeks at a time?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like this, anyway. I mean, I’ve had bad days and stressful stretches before, like anyone, but I can’t really remember another time where it went on for weeks and felt this heavy. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I have, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but things I used to really care about just feel… far away now. I used to paint, and I liked cooking big meals, and I’d run before jobs sometimes. I was also showing up for theater rehearsals.

Now all of that feels like chores from somebody else’s life, if that makes sense. Like if I miss it, I don’t really care the way I should. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed a change in your appetite?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I mean, I’m not trying to lose weight or anything, but most days I kind of forget to eat until it’s late, or I’ll make something and then only take a few bites because I feel sick. My work pants have been looser, so… I suppose it’s changed. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Has this depression continued for more than six months after your husband’s injury changed your day-to-day life?

Yes… yeah, it has. I wish I could say it was just a rough adjustment period, but it’s been longer than six months. It started a few months after my husband got hurt, and it’s been… about a year and two months now, I think. Does that answer it okay?
Have you been feeling worthless?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to say it like that, because I know it sounds… extreme. But yes.

I keep thinking I’m the reason things got worse. Like with my husband, and the crew losing work, and clients’ homes getting messed up… it all feels like it traces back to me somehow. Like I poison everything I touch. I know that’s probably not the “right” way to think about it, but it feels true a lot of the time.

And then I think maybe I deserve whatever happens to me because of it. Is that… is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Do you believe you actually caused your husband’s injury?

I… I don’t know if “caused” is the right word. I know that probably sounds irrational.

But I keep feeling like it’s my fault somehow. Like if I had done something different, he wouldn’t have gotten worse, and then the crew wouldn’t have lost work, and clients’ homes wouldn’t have gotten messed up. It all feels like it points back to me… like I poison everything I touch.

I’m sorry, that sounds awful. I just… I feel like I deserve whatever happens after that. Does that make sense?
Do you believe, deep down, that you truly caused these bad things to happen?

Deep down… yes. I mean, I know it probably doesn’t sound logical, and I’m not trying to be dramatic, but it feels that way.

I keep thinking if I hadn’t… if I’d done things differently, my husband wouldn’t have gotten worse, and then the crew wouldn’t have lost work, and those clients’ homes wouldn’t have been messed up. It’s like it all comes back to me somehow.

I feel like I poisoned everything I touched… and then part of me thinks I deserve whatever happens because of it. Is that… is that what you mean?
Has anyone tried to reassure you that your husband’s injury and the other problems were not your fault, but you still know for certain that they were?

Yes… people have tried to tell me it wasn’t my fault. My husband has said it, and other people sort of say, “You couldn’t have caused all that.”

And I nod, because I know that’s what I’m supposed to do, and I don’t want to argue with everybody. But inside… I don’t really believe them. It still feels certain to me that I’m the reason he got worse, and then the crew lost work, and those homes got messed up.

I know it probably sounds wrong, or too much, but it feels like I poisoned everything I touched. Like… if all that came from me, then maybe I deserve whatever happens after. Is that okay to say?
Do you believe with complete certainty that these bad things happened because of you?

I… I think so. I don’t want to sound like I’m blaming myself just to get attention or anything, but yes, it feels certain inside.

Like my husband got worse because of me somehow, and then the crew losing work and the clients’ homes getting messed up… I keep tracing it all back to me. Like I ruined it, or I poisoned everything I touched.

I know you might tell me that’s not how it works, and I’m trying to understand that, but it doesn’t feel true to me. It feels like I deserve whatever happens because of it.
Do you believe, with absolute certainty, that you poisoned everything you touched and caused these bad things to happen?

Yes… I mean, I know “absolute certainty” sounds extreme, and I don’t want to say it wrong, but… inside, yes.

I keep coming back to the same thing: my husband got worse because of me somehow, then the crew lost work, and then those clients’ homes got messed up. It feels like I poisoned everything I touched.

I know that probably doesn’t make sense to other people, and I’m trying to be reasonable, but it feels true. And if I did all that, then… I guess I deserve whatever happens to me. Is that what you’re asking?
